announcements.text: Hi everyone! Welcome to course 02808 Personal Data Interaction. Here are a few practical remarks about the course and action points before lecture 1.  Time, place and schedule The lectures takes place on Wednesdays from 9.00 in building 324 auditorium 040. A tentative schedule for the course is available in DTU Learn.  Personal Data Interaction & Personal Informatics    The course is about personal data interaction (also known as personal informatics), a subject that has gained a tremendous interest in the last decade due to technological developments including smaller, faster, and cheaper computing and sensing technologies that enable new types of data about humans to be collected. The course is about building and evaluating user interfaces that support people in learning something valuable about themselves based on acquired personal data. This has broad application in areas including health, treatment, well-being, training, performance, learning, etc.   Building human-centered personal informatics systems    This course is part of the master's program in Human-Centered AI, and in this course we have a strong focus on the human-centered part, that is, how machines can augment human capabilities. Our emphasis is on how we can build and evaluate machines and software that can assist or augment human beings in reasoning based on personal data about or related to themselves. Therefore there is a strong focus on the user interface between the technology and the human users of that technology. As a key component in building such augmentation systems is the interaction between the human user and the system, the course is framed within the research area Human Computer Interaction.  ACTION POINTS BEFORE LECTURE 1:  Course material      The course literature consists of two textbooks on Human-Computer Interaction along with a number of research papers. The papers will be made available through DTU Learn. We will use excerpts from these two text books, which are both available online:  Hornbæk et al. (2025) Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction, which is available here: https://introductiontohci.org/ and as a downloadable PDF here: https://global.oup.com/academic/product/introduction-to-human-computer-interaction-9780192864543?cc=fi&lang=en& Mackenzie (2013) Human-Computer Interaction, which is available online (in PDF format) if you use this link below to login via the DTU library:   [ https://www-sciencedirect-com.proxy.findit.cvt.dk/book/9780124058651/human-computer-interaction ]( https://www-sciencedirect-com.proxy.findit.cvt.dk/book/9780124058651/human-computer-interaction) Download your own personal data    During the course you will be working with your own personal data. We will do that from the first week. Therefore I strongly encourage you to already now look into how you can download/export your own personal data (e.g., activity tracking data, fitness data, sleep data, location tracking data, messaging data, music listening data, ... or whatever you would find interesting to work with). See the "Getting started with data visualization" module for some suggestions for how you can download/export your personal data sets: https://learn.inside.dtu.dk/d2l/le/lessons/296264/lessons/1153215 Create an account for Observable Notebooks For creating data visualizations and building prototypes we will be working with the tool Observable Notebooks. You will receive an invite for the Observable team "DTU". You can create a free account for Observable notebooks on: https://observablehq.com/get-started See you all on Wednesday! Best,   Jakob

announcements.text: Given the diversity of students in the course and their varying experiences with DTU exams, we wish to remind you of the exam format and highlight the importance of completing the  Answer Sheet correctly. The exam format is "no aids" (c.f. DTU rules), multiple choice (with negative marking ), 4 hours, and on-campus. The  only allowed  aids are: Two A4 sheets of  handwritten notes (an exception to the default no aids rules). Any other type of notes, as printed notes prepared on a tablet, is not allowed. Standard dictionaries in book form (e.g. DA-EN, DA-EN) You should, of course, bring your student ID, basic writing tools such as pencils/pens, eraser, ruler, and perhaps also a drawing compass (“passer” in Danish) - and whatever necessities you need (snack, drink, etc.) Note that any type of electronic device is not allowed, i.e., calculator , computer, tablet, etc.   Exam location (individual):  https://eksamensplan.dtu.dk/  ( make a note of your building/room and table no. ! )   Exam script : The exam script will be provided on paper along with a separate  Answer Sheet . Blank paper for intermediate calculations will be available in the exam room.   Hand-in and Answer Sheet : You must only hand in the  Answer Sheet (the provided and preformatted single A4 sheet). It is  critical  that you complete and fill in the required information ( building/room, table no., and student ID ) on the  Answer Sheet   – we will typically not accept the submission if any of this information is missing! announcements.preview: Dear all, In week 12 we will discuss various topics related to so-called representation learning. Aside from general motivation and applications, we will mainly focus on two key ideas in representatio
announcements.text: Dear all, In week 12 we will discuss various topics related to so-called representation learning. Aside from general motivation and applications, we will mainly focus on two key ideas in representation learning: I ) Learning low-dimensional representations -    PCA (from week 3) -    t-SNE [1]  -    Laplacian eigenmaps* [2] II ) Learning consistent representations via auto-encoding -    Neural networks for auto-encoding (with regularization)  Preparation : We recommend you prepare by reviewing chapter on PCA (ch 3), chapter on neural networks (ch 15 incl. 15.4.3) and skim the original t-SNE article [1]. You are also welcome to study the Laplacian eigenmaps paper [2, section 1], but it is not examinable. We expect to upload the preview slides and Python exercise on Monday afternoon. [1] Visualizing Data using t-SNE, van der Maarten et al., JMLR, 2008, https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume9/vandermaaten08a/vandermaaten08a.pdf [2] Laplacian Eigenmaps for Dimensionality Reduction and Data Representation, Belkin et al., Neural Computation, 2003, https://www2.imm.dtu.dk/projects/manifold/Papers/Laplacian.pdf

announcements.text: Hey Folks, Since posting Assignment 2, I've heard from some of you with concerns. Therefore, I ask you to use your good judgement to select what parts of the exercises you want to use on in order to answer the more abstract questions posed in Assignment 2. And now for a super important point! When you answer Assignment 2, we are still expecting that you clearly state what question you're answering, coherent explanatory text, nice plots with labeled axes & captions, explanation of choices, and all the other good stuff from https://github.com/suneman/socialgraphs2025/wiki/Assignments . announcements.preview: Dear all students of the course Quantitative methods to assess sustainability (Polytechnical Foundation) We hope you have had a great summer and welcome back to semester start! This course is designed
announcements.text: Dear all students of the course Quantitative methods to assess sustainability (Polytechnical Foundation) We hope you have had a great summer and welcome back to semester start! This course is designed with the purpose of creating active teaching sessions, where the teaching sessions are focused on the act of quantifying, analyzing and assessing the sustainability of products, services or systems. The assumption is therefor that you come prepared to the teaching sessions, so that you are ready to study the exercises and cases together with the teachers and the teaching assistants. You can read more about the preparation required for each module in the specific module descriptions (see overview in Schedule ). Before module 1 about Sustainability concepts you should: Watch the 4 video lectures Study the self-assessment Watch the different case introductions and read the case descriptions ( Content → 0.2 Case descriptions ) and consider which case study you would like to enroll into. The enrollment opens in the end of module 1.  Your case study group should during the course submit task 1, task 2 and task 3. Each individual student should give peer feedback to two submissions of task 1 and two submissions of task 2. Get an overview of the course  Deadlines . We use different teaching rooms in the general modules (week 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12) and the case study modules (week 3, 9 and 13). See the overview of the  teaching rooms . You can read more about the course in the course description and the extended course description . We are looking forward to the teaching sessions. On behalf of the general module teachers, case study teachers and teaching assistants Best regards Couse responsibles David Lusseau and Stig Irving Olsen

announcements.title: Welcome to 02452 Fall 2025
announcements.preview: Dear 02452 Course Participant, Welcome to 02452 Machine Learning - Fall 2025 edition! Lectures and exercises take place on Tuesday afternoons from 13:00 - 17:00, starting on the 2nd of September. The
announcements.text: Dear 02452 Course Participant, Welcome to 02452 Machine Learning - Fall 2025 edition! Lectures and exercises take place on Tuesday afternoons from 13:00 - 17:00, starting on the 2nd of September. The lecture session is scheduled for 13:00 - 15:00, followed by the exercise session from 15:00 - 17:00. You can attend the weekly lecture in person or watch the live stream via the Zoom link on DTU Learn. The lecture will take place in building 116, auditorium 081 (275 seats), and streamed to auditorium 082 (100 seats). Unfortunately, the total number of seats is insufficient to support the whole class (~500 students), and seats will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. The exercise rooms listed on the public webpage can be used to stream the lecture via Zoom using the link on DTU Learn. The weekly exercises will take place in dedicated rooms/locations listed on the course website and in the syllabus. Teaching assistants will be present to guide and assist you. We highly recommend attending in person, as students who engage with the course tend to perform better. The curriculum is based on lecture notes available on DTU Learn as a book. The reading material for the first lecture on Tuesday, the 2nd of September, is Chapter 1, Chapter 2, and Chapter 7 in the file 02450_Book.pdf (found under Content > Book > 02450_Book.pdf). Please bring your own laptop to the lectures and exercises to engage with the in-class quizzes. Throughout the semester, we will provide Python Notebooks for the exercises, where you will need to complete the code. This code will be useful for the project reports. We have already uploaded Exercise 0 (see Content > Exercises) to help you get started with Python Notebooks, which also contains a brief refresher/intro on the programming language. This is critical if you do not have experience with Python and/or Notebooks. We recommend following the instructions in Exercise 0 before the first exercise session to ensure your setup is working from the start. Use the Discussion Forum to raise any issues. We encourage you to use the Discussion Forum (i.e., Piazza) to post questions (which can be anonymous), provide answers, and discuss aspects of the material for the benefit of the whole class. More information about the course, syllabus, reading material, and exercises can be found on the public course homepage: http://www.compute.dtu.dk/courses/02452 and the course handbook (Content > Course Handbook > 02452coursebook.pdf), which outlines the formal requirements and rules. The website also contains a list of recommended homework problems for each week. We highly recommend you study the assigned readings and attempt the problems before attending the lectures. We look forward to meeting you on the 2nd of September at 13:00, either in person or online! All the best, Georgios and the rest of the 02452 team

announcements.text: Dear student, A very warm welcome to 02810 (previously 02809) UX Design Prototyping, Fall 2025! I am exited to be seeing you next week, Monday September 1st at 08:00 where the lecture begins in building 306 auditorium 035 . Unfortunately, and very regrettably, the room only seats 194 students (and we currently have at least twice as many signed up), so some of you will have to show up in the group area in 358 (where rooms 064 to 072 are booked for us) and watch the lecture  via this zoom link on your own computer. I'll do what I can to include zoom comments and questions also, and we'll take turns so that all of you will have a chance to attend some of the lectures "live". Perhaps for this Mondays lecture, primarily those of you with a last name that starts with A up to and including L will go to the main auditorium in 306, and those of you with a last name that starts with M up to Å consider going to 358 This would likely fill the auditorium in 306... so in case you arrive to 306 and don't find a seat, please then continue to 358 instead. Also, it may be advisable to not show up at the last minute :-) I very much apologize for this inconvenience; although there are 3 slightly larger lecture halls at DTU, we simply don't have a lecture hall that could hold all of us! After the lecture we will immediately proceed to supervised group work in 358 until 12:00. There should be sufficient space for us in the 9 rooms assigned (064, 065, 066, 067, 068, 069, 070, 071 and 072 -- see this map if you don't know where it is). We will use learn.inside.dtu.dk for course related information and relevant material, which will be continuously updated through this week and the rest of the course weeks. If you find any issues that e.g. prevents you from accessing links or read the provided information, kindly let us know! There is some important information that is relevant for all to read in the Course Overview area, and you can find the first week materials under 25.01 Modelling Needs and Solutions , including links that help you to prepare. Note that this content will be updated on a weekly basis, so it's good to check for any late minute changes at the beginning of each week -- last year's material is currently there as a placeholder, so you know  approximately what to expect from the course. In particular, I would like to point out that you should form groups of 6 persons ( with different backgrounds , so avoid forming groups where all have the same study line) and write your study number, name and study line in this google sheet . There is also going to be a channel for the course (details in Course Overview ); we will use that actively for e.g. questions during the week, contact to the TAs, relevant general information or clarifications and group to group interactions. See you all next week, -- Per.

studyAnnouncements.text:
Below are the deadlines for enrolment in and withdrawal from 3-week courses in January, as well as information about the lottery process.

Please note that there is a difference between the deadline for post-enrolment for 3-week courses and the deadline for withdrawal from 3-week courses. Read more below.
Be aware that special registration rules/deadlines apply for part-time students and guest students. You can find the deadlines on DTU's website www.dtu.dk .
If you are enrolled as a part-time student at DTU Learn for Life, other deadlines and rules also apply. You can stay informed under your class at DTU Inside and on the website https://www.dtu.dk/english/education/continuing-education

Deadlines for registration for and withdrawal from 3-week courses
Period of enrolment: 15/11 2026 – 1/12 2026
Period of post-enrolment: 13/12 2026 – 5/1 2027
Deadline for withdrawal June: 8/1 2027
Registration and withdrawal
You must register for courses using the Study Planner . The deadline for registration during the ordinary registration period is 1/12 2026 at 11.59 pm.
Please be aware of the following:
If a course spans two semesters, you should only register for the first part. Your registration will automatically be transferred to the second semester. That means if you are enrolled in a 13+3 course, your registration for the 3-week course will automatically be transferred.
When your course registration has been approved, you will be able to see it in your study plan, as the individual courses are marked with a tick. When you register, you can choose to print a registration receipt, which will be sent to your study email. You can use the receipt or a screenshot from your study plan as documentation that you have registered for the course in question.

Starting Thursday, October 15 you can register for and withdraw from winter exams. You register for and withdraw from exams on student.dtu.dk under ‘Tools’.
You are automatically registered for the exam in the courses you have been signed up for during the 13-week period. You can see your exam registrations on student.dtu.dk under ‘Tools/My exams’.
During the registration period, you also have the option to register for exams or re-exams in courses for which you are not registered for teaching. You register for exams or re-exams at www.tilmelding.dtu.dk.
If you want to register for a re-exam, you must register for the exam via the same link as for the ordinary exam registration.
If you do not wish to take the exam in winter 2026 for a course in which you have been enrolled during the 13-week period, you must withdraw from the exam. Deadline for withdrawal and binding courses

You can apply for an exemption to be released from the exam registration if special circumstances exist, cf. the current exemption rules. studyAnnouncements.title: Study announcement s1921: Changes in DTU’s study rules for the academic year 2026/2027
studyAnnouncements.teaser: As of September 1, 2026, revised study rules will come into effect. Below, you can read about the changes. Each section includes a link to student.dtu.dk, where you can read the specific rules.
studyAnnouncements.text:
In the academic year 2025/2026, we announced expected changes to DTU’s exam rules for the 2026/2027 academic year. A major revision of the exam rules has been postponed and will instead be coordinated with DTU’s work on examination formats.
Only a limited number of changes have been made to the study rules this year. However, several wording adjustments have been implemented throughout the study rules to make communication about DTU’s rules and procedures more user-friendly. These revisions are not described in this notice but can be viewed at: https://student.dtu.dk/studieregler
If you have any questions about what the rule changes mean for you, you can contact the study guidance. DTU’s guidance services are available at student.dtu.dk under ‘Help and guidance’ here - https://student.dtu.dk/en/help-and-guidance/study-guidance
1. Exemption to begin the internship in the Bachelor of Engineering programme
From now on, exemptions allowing students in the Bachelor of Engineering (BEng.) programme to commence their internship before all prerequisites have been fulfilled will be granted by the Exemption Committee for the BEng. programme. Consequently, you must apply to the committee if you wish to obtain an exemption for commencing the internship or an exemption from the internship requirement.

This change can be found in DTU’s rules on exemption under “Commencement of engineering internship - https://student.dtu.dk/en/rules/Exemption/Commencement-of-engineering-internship and is also included in the programme specifications for the BEng. programme - https://student.dtu.dk/studieordninger#diplomingenioer

Applications for exemptions must be submitted through DTU’s exemption system: www.dispensation.dtu.dk

Information on how to apply and what your application must contain can be found at: https://student.dtu.dk/en/rules/exemption#general-requirements-for-your-application

2.      Guest students’ access to courses
It is no longer described in the study rules that an instructor can exclude a guest student from a course on the grounds of insufficient academic qualifications or language proficiency. Once you have been admitted to a course as a guest student, exclusion may only take place in cases involving violations of DTU’s disciplinary rules.

Admission requirements for guest students can be found in the study rules under “Guest Students”: https://student.dtu.dk/en/rules/guest-students#Admission

3.      New practice for allowing a quick re-exam
DTU tillader at du som studerende kan søge om en hurtig reeksamen, hvis du enten er syg eller ikke består den sidste afsluttende eksamen i den eksamenstermin, hvor din uddannelse skulle være afsluttet. Reglerne for hurtig reeksamen er ikke ændret, men formuleringen er præciseret, så det er tydeligt, hvornår der er mulighed for at få godkendt en hurtig reeksamen, herunder hvad betingelserne er.

DTU allows students to apply for a quick re-exam if they are unable to attend the final examination required to complete their study programme due to illness or if they fail the exam during the examination period that concludes the study programme. The rules governing quick re-examinations have not changed; however, the wording has been clarified to make it clearer when a quick re-exam may be approved and which conditions must be met.

Information about the new criteria and application procedure can be found under “Re-exams” here: https://student.dtu.dk/en/rules/Exam/Re-exams#Special

4.      Information: new placement of admission and credit transfer regulations
Information regarding programme changes, as well as information on re-admission and re-enrolment, is now available exclusively on www.dtu.dk under “How to apply”: https://www.dtu.dk/english/education

Information on deadlines, previously completed courses, and examination attempts used for credit transfer from prior education, which was previously included in the DTU study rules, has now been added to the relevant pages on www.dtu.dk. During autumn 2026, all admission pages for DTU’s degree programmes will be revised to provide students and applicants with a more consistent communication experience.

All credit transfer regulations, including credit transfer from prior education, credit transfer during a degree programme, and credit transfer in connection with study abroad, are now exclusively in DTU’s study rules under “Credit transfer, Studying abroad”: https://student.dtu.dk/en/rules/Credit-transfer-studying-abroad

You must bring your student card as proof of identity at the exams. If you do not have your student card with you, you have to produce some other form of photo ID. If you cannot display photo ID, you need to contact the Study Administration in person before the exam starts. The Study Administration is located in building 101A at Lyngby Campus and in the Study Information at Ballerup Campus.

Read more about proof of identity at exams at student.dtu.dk under “Exam/Exam guides”. 

Students at DTU Continuing Education
If you are enrolled at a part time education at DTU Continuing Education other deadlines and rules apply. Read more at DTU Inside or at dtu.dk under ‘Continuing education’.

Students in Biomedical Engineering (BSc and MSc)
If you are enrolled in the programme Biomedical Engineering, please note that you will automatically be registered for the exams on your UCPH, SUND courses. If you want to register for an UCPH exam without being registered on the course, you do this via DTU. You also need to withdrawal from an exam via DTU. If you want to enrol for a reexam, you need to do this via the self-service on KUnet. Information about deadlines and schedules are also available on KUnet.

If you wish to begin your your Bachelor of Engineering project before fulfilling all prerequisites, you must apply for an exemption. You can read more about the application requirements at student.dtu.dk
From 1 February 2026, the Exemption Board for BEng programmes (DMDU) will handle these applications. Previously, the head of study for the individual study programme could grant exemptions, but this responsibility has now been transferred to DMDU.
This change means that the processing of exemption applications for starting a Bachelor of Engineering project before all prerequisites are met will now follow the same principles as for bachelor’s and master’s students. Similar cases are already handled by the CMDU Exemption Board.
You can find additional information as well as track-specific requirements for starting your master’s engineering project in your study regulations here: https://student.dtu.dk/en/programme-specifications
